items.title: Number of subsets of a finite set

question.text: Why does a finite set with n elements have exactly 2 to the power n subsets?

from_notes.text: Theorem 1.7. If a finite set S has n elements, then it has 2^{n} subsets. Proof: for each element x_i, there are two choices: include it or exclude it, so the total number of subsets is 2 \cdot 2 \cdots 2 = 2^{n}.

explanation.text: Each subset corresponds to choosing independently whether to include each element or not, producing 2^{n} distinct subsets that correspond to binary strings of length n.

items.title: Basic principle of mathematical induction
question: What are the three essential steps to prove a statement P(n) for all integers n greater or equal to n0 using mathematical induction?

parts: To prove the statement P(n) for all integers n ≥ n0 by induction, we perform (1) base case: prove P(n0), (2) induction hypothesis: fix n ≥ n0 and assume P(n) true, (3) induction step: prove P(n + 1) using the hypothesis.

Suppose we want to prove a statement P(n) for every integer n ≥ n0 . We prove it in three steps: 1. Base case: prove P(n0) . 2. Induction hypothesis: fix an arbitrary integer n ≥ n0 and assume that P(n) is true. 3. Induction step: using the induction hypothesis, prove that P(n + 1) is true.

If \(a < b\), choose a large enough natural number \(n\) so that \(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{n} < b - a\). Then if \(a \in \mathbb{Q} \)take \(a + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{n}\); if \(a \notin \mathbb{Q} \)take \(a + \frac{1}{n}\); these lie between \(a\) and \(b\) and are irrational.
